activity.title: 🎉 Wrapping up Day 3: Engineering, and with it, the final night of VISA: The Insider Case, I keep coming back to one feeling: gratitude. Over the past three days, this series became more than just a set of career panels. It became a space where students could hear honest stories about what it really takes to grow into competitive fields — not just the highlights, but also the uncertainty, the setbacks, and the discipline behind the progress. ⚙️ For Engineering Day, we were incredibly grateful to be joined by Hung Pham , Linh Ha , and Vien Nguyen , who each brought a different but equally valuable perspective. Hung Pham helped students think more intentionally about the CS journey early on: exploring different paths, building experience before chasing prestige, and taking freshman and sophomore years seriously as a time to experiment, apply, and grow. Linh Ha shared a perspective that felt especially real and grounding — that the path is not linear, going from 0 to 1 is often the hardest part, and consistency, mentorship, and trusting your own timeline matter more than comparison. Vien Nguyen challenged students to think more deeply about what makes a project meaningful: not just building something that works, but understanding the problem, designing thoughtfully, communicating clearly, and turning projects into real stories of engineering growth. To everyone who attended across all three days, thank you for showing up with curiosity, openness, and energy. Your questions, conversations, and willingness to learn are what made this series feel alive. 🙌 And to the Vietnamese International Student Association at USF e-board, thank you all for the care and work behind the scenes that made all of this possible. If there is one thing this 3-day series reminded me, it is this: no path is perfectly clear at the beginning, but hearing honest stories from people a few steps ahead can make the journey feel a lot more possible. 💙 ✨ Thank you to every speaker, attendee, and team member who helped make VISA: The Insider Case so meaningful. This was a special one.

Amazon is doing 5 day RTO, but it's not enough. If you want max productivity you have to go further. At Central, we put our employees on regimented diet plans, fitness routines, and sleep programs. If you want to perform like a professional, you need to train like one. Starting today, all employees will be required to sleep in-office 7 days a week in our cryogenic recovery pods. We're hiring engineers so if this sounds like a good fit, fly to my house and present your resume and current meal plan.

For the fourth time I feel like I'm writing the same post, but this time it's actually different. Instead of joining Uber as an intern, I'll now be joining as a full time software engineer in SF. It's been a journey. My first internship at Uber was back in 2023, when I was still in community college, writing code by hand, and had major imposter syndrome being in a room full of interns from top universities. Now I've just graduated from UCSD with a bachelor's in Computer Science, and I've swapped out the self doubt for a genuine drive to keep leveling up as an engineer. I’m excited for this next chapter in my life and I have so many people to thank for it including my family, team members, mentors, managers and recruiters. Here's to the next chapter. 🚀🚗 #LifeAtUber #OfferAccepted

I Quitted this year YC Startup School... But I don't regret it. This time last year, I was attending the first ever YC startup school in the world. Being one of the pioneering participants bring me a very exciting and unique experience. But this year, I'm not going there. Instead, I spent a whole month in Vietnam, went back and forth between cities, met a bunch of new friends, and learned a lot of new things. During the time, I was lucky enough to attend the GRAB the Future Hackathon, which eventually granted me a Data Analyst intern at Grab. Later, I went to the Agentic AI Build Week from GenAI Fund, where I built and integrated Muster Task Delegator into internal operations at KT One. Closing the month was an amazing time at the 2nd SEA Quantathon in Vietnam, where KT One was able to secured a 3rd place along with investment opportunities. Thank you for making my summer extraordinaries, my G Duc-Kha Vu , Long Le , Marc Jermaine Pontiveros, and also with a lot of friends we talked along the way. P/s: First time on live broadcast, would prepare better next time!

Today was my last day at the University of South Florida . Over the past three years as an instructor in mechanical engineering, I have learned so much about myself as an educator and as a person. I've made incredible friends, interacted with thousands of students, and grew as an engineer. To my colleagues: thank you for the support you have given me (especially to Miguel Goni Rodrigo and Karim Nohra who have become incredible friends since this journey began). Having colleagues to bounce ideas off of, look to for guidance, or simply to vent to makes the job easier and a lot more fun. To my students: thank you for everything. You were the reasons I wanted to come to work every day. I appreciate your desire to learn, your motivation, and your friendship. And despite being your professor, I have learned so much from you all as well: whether in engineering, mentoring, or simply humor that I am too much of a millennial to understand, it has shaped me more than you will ever know. You are all strong and will do incredible things in your lives: please keep in touch so I can hear of all your successes. Lastly, to my wife Samantha Korn : thank you for your patience and support during this whole time. Being an instructor requires a lot more time than just teaching in a lecture hall; it requires preparation, grading, office hours, meetings, etc. You have been my rock and I am glad to continue this journey with you to North Carolina, where I will begin as an adjunct professor in the Department of Mechanical & Aerospace Engineering at North Carolina State University . Thank you again from the bottom of my heart. I hope to see my USF family again soon. Go Bulls!
